facts.fact_source: Parsed from the URDF at the pinned upstream commit: link/joint elements and inertial masses. Every joint in the file is fixed and the propeller links carry zero mass — a rigid-body model with no spinning-rotor dynamics.

specimen.annotation_note: This entry arrived by import, not by hand: the description was located by robot_descriptions (module cf2_description), which downloads UTIAS's gym-pybullet-drones repository; the facts above were parsed out of its cf2p.urdf, which describes the Crazyflie 2.0 (see the version note under honesty). Nothing here was gated — importing a description is not a verdict.
honesty: VERSION: the upstream file describes the Crazyflie 2.0, not this entry's Crazyflie 2.1 — the two are not silently equated. The file's total mass is 27 g (the 2.0's figure); the 2.1 datasheet takeoff weight is 29 g. The entry keeps the 2.1 datasheet figures; the specimen records the 2.0 file's numbers, with the difference stated here.
Gate status stays NOT_GATED: the motion gate grades wheeled ground robots, and no flight gate exists yet.
The parts kit stays undefined (kit: null in catalog/parts-kits.json): the kit generator builds wheeled kits from a spec's wheel block, and this robot has no wheels.
The file is a rigid model: all five joints are fixed and the propeller links carry zero mass — it supports geometry and mass bookkeeping, not rotor dynamics.

The license recorded here is the license of the gym-pybullet-drones repository that carries the file, read from its LICENSE. Bitcraze publishes the Crazyflie design files themselves as open-source hardware — see the entry provenance; the two statements are about different artifacts.
The URDF tree is not vendored into this repo — the manifest pins the upstream repo, commit and URDF path.
